## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (53%)** · Ambiguous: Normal vs Benign · Read in turn
Invasive probability is under 1%; Normal and Benign are not separable [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 53%, Normal 46%, InSitu 1%, Invasive 0% | Near coin-flip |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.95 / 92nd percentile | Input not flagged |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes | Same top class |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 Benign | Neighbors lean Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules** (regions 5, 6, 10) · ↓ invasive · Strongest score here, but spot check failed [F2] · Unreliable
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 5, 6, 10) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical score; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F3] · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Score below typical; little push toward invasive · Validated
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 7) · ↑ invasive · Typical score; near-zero contribution · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI (−0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules is Unreliable (0/20).

## Could be wrong if
- The image is a simulated JPEG-degraded variant; compression may blur Normal-versus-Benign cues.
- Four of five similar reference cases are Normal, not Benign.

## Check on the slide
1. **Region 7:** strongest invasive-associated concept scores; mitoses (0/20) and necrosis (3/20) are unreliable.
2. **Regions 9, 10:** older per-region probe gives 72% and 67% invasive, versus under 1% whole-image; confirm benign.
3. **Regions 5, 6, 10:** verify two-layered epithelium and gland formation, since the lobule concept failed its spot check.
